text: Remove the tab×hour cross from experiment 2 to restore the validated seven-field request-context FM.
rationale: Experiment 2's only added tab×hour field reduced primary from 0.60143 in experiment 1 to 0.60065. Reverting that isolated harmful addition is the lowest-risk recovery hypothesis.
exact_ablation: Remove exactly the tab_hour categorical field from experiment 2, retaining user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, duration bucket, hour, weekday, FM architecture, binary cross-entropy loss, optimizer, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.0008 to +0.0020, recovering the within-user ordering loss observed after adding tab_hour.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0000 to +0.0005, recovering the small top-five regression observed after adding tab_hour.

text: Increase FM interaction dimension from 16 to 32 for the validated seven-field request-context model.
rationale: The supported request-context main effects improve ranking, while the explicit tab×hour field was not beneficial. A larger latent interaction space may represent useful existing field interactions without introducing a sparse hand-built cross.
exact_ablation: Change only interaction_dimension from 16 to 32 in experiment 1; retain its seven input fields, binary cross-entropy loss, optimizer settings, seed, batch size, epoch limit, and early-stopping policy.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.0002 to +0.0015 from more expressive user-item-context interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0001 to +0.0012 if additional interaction capacity resolves a small number of top-five inversions.

text: Increase FM L2 regularization to reduce sparse-ID and context overfitting.
rationale: The model contains high-cardinality user, item, and author IDs, and the sparse tab×hour expansion hurt validation performance. Stronger regularization may improve temporal generalization without adding any feature.
exact_ablation: Change only l2 from 0.000001 to 0.00001 in experiment 1; retain all seven fields, interaction dimension, learning rate, optimizer, seed, batching, loss, and stopping policy unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.0000 to +0.0012 through less overfit sparse entity interactions.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0002 to +0.0008 because regularization can either improve top-five generalization or flatten useful score differences.

text: Decrease FM L2 regularization to allow stronger fitted entity and context interactions.
rationale: Experiment 1's strongest performance comes from a compact seven-field model. If its current regularization is constraining interaction magnitudes, a smaller penalty could improve within-user item separation; this directly contrasts the stronger-regularization hypothesis.
exact_ablation: Change only l2 from 0.000001 to 0.0000001 in experiment 1; retain all seven fields, interaction dimension, learning rate, optimizer, seed, batching, loss, and stopping policy unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0003 to +0.0010 if retained entity interactions become more discriminative.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0005 to +0.0012 if greater score separation improves top-five ordering.

text: Lower the FM learning rate from 0.001 to 0.0005 for a less noisy optimization trajectory.
rationale: The tab×hour change produced a small decline rather than a large signal, so an optimization-only change provides an interpretable check for whether the baseline checkpoint is sensitive to update noise without changing features or objective.
exact_ablation: Change only learning_rate from 0.001 to 0.0005 in experiment 1; retain model size, seven fields, L2, optimizer type, seed, batch size, maximum epochs, patience, and binary cross-entropy loss unchanged.

expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0002 to +0.0008 because slower learning may preserve or weaken top-five score separation.

text: Raise the FM learning rate from 0.001 to 0.002 to test for under-training under the current early-stop schedule.
rationale: The model is selected by an internal ranking checkpoint. A single higher learning rate may reach a better ranking region within the same epoch budget, while leaving all data and features untouched.
exact_ablation: Change only learning_rate from 0.001 to 0.002 in experiment 1; retain model size, seven fields, L2, optimizer type, seed, batch size, maximum epochs, patience, and binary cross-entropy loss unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0008 to +0.0010; faster learning may improve separation but can overshoot.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0010 to +0.0012; sharper score differences may help or destabilize top-five ranking.

text: Replace binary cross-entropy with within-user pairwise logistic ranking loss.
rationale: The official objective is entirely within-user ordering, and experiment 2 has GAUC 0.66560 versus nDCG@5 0.53569, leaving a notable top-five gap. Pairwise training directly optimizes positive-versus-negative ordering within each user.
exact_ablation: Replace only the binary cross-entropy training loss in experiment 1 with a uniformly sampled within-user positive-negative pairwise logistic loss; retain seven fields, FM architecture, optimizer hyperparameters, seed, epochs, and model-selection metric unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.0005 to +0.0025 from direct optimization of within-user positive-negative order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0002 to +0.0020 if pairwise corrections move positives into the top five.

text: Replace binary cross-entropy with a top-heavy within-user pairwise loss that samples negatives from the model's highest-scoring candidates.
rationale: The large tab 0 diagnostic slice has nDCG@5 of 0.06331 despite GAUC of 0.58556, and medium-frequency items have GAUC 0.71277 but nDCG@5 0.24497. This indicates broad ordering can coexist with poor top-five placement, motivating a top-focused loss.
exact_ablation: Replace only the binary cross-entropy loss in experiment 1 with a within-user pairwise logistic loss that, for each positive, samples the current highest-scoring eligible negative in that user's training impressions; retain all fields, architecture, optimizer settings, seed, and selection metric unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0005 to +0.0015 because hard-negative emphasis can sacrifice broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0005 to +0.0030 by concentrating updates on likely top-five inversions.

text: Use inverse user-impression-count weights in binary cross-entropy so highly active users do not dominate training updates.
rationale: Official nDCG@5 is macro-averaged across users, whereas unweighted row loss gives more influence to users with many training impressions. User-frequency segments show differentiated behavior, so a user-balanced loss is a ranking-aligned training ablation.
exact_ablation: Replace only unweighted binary cross-entropy in experiment 1 with binary cross-entropy weighted by the reciprocal of each user's count of training impressions, normalized to mean weight one; retain all model, feature, optimizer, seed, and schedule settings unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0003 to +0.0015 because user balancing may trade dominant-user fit for macro ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0000 to +0.0020 because the training weighting better matches macro per-user top-five evaluation.

text: Replace the FM interaction layer with a field-aware factorization machine while retaining the seven validated fields.
rationale: The current FM shares each feature embedding across all counterpart fields. Field-aware embeddings can distinguish user-item, user-author, and item-context interactions without adding unsupported feature groups or sparse manual crosses.
exact_ablation: Replace only the standard FM interaction parameterization in experiment 1 with field-aware FM embeddings; retain exactly the same seven encoded fields, binary cross-entropy loss, optimizer settings, seed, batch size, and stopping procedure.

expected_effect.GAUC: +0.0002 to +0.0020 from more specific cross-field within-user discrimination.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: +0.0001 to +0.0018 if field-specific interactions improve top-five item placement.

text: Replace the FM interaction layer with a two-layer DeepFM-style interaction MLP over the existing field embeddings.
rationale: The request-context screen supports main effects, but the manually materialized tab×hour categorical cross regressed. A nonlinear interaction layer may learn only supported combinations while retaining the same leakage-safe inputs.
exact_ablation: Replace only the FM second-order interaction term in experiment 1 with a two-layer MLP over the concatenated embeddings of its existing seven fields; retain field inputs, binary cross-entropy loss, optimizer type, seed, and checkpoint selection metric unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0005 to +0.0020 because extra nonlinearity can learn useful interactions or overfit the short temporal window.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0005 to +0.0025 because nonlinear context ranking may improve or degrade top-five order.

text: Remove duration bucket from the seven-field request-context FM.
rationale: Training-only screening found the content-duration feature family harmful, with primary lift -0.01044. Although the deployed duration bucket is a compact impression-time field rather than the whole screened family, an isolated removal tests whether it is adding unstable duration effects.
exact_ablation: Remove exactly the dur_bucket field from experiment 1, retaining user_id, video_id, author_id, tab, hour, weekday, FM architecture, loss, optimizer, seed, and training schedule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: -0.0005 to +0.0015 if removing a harmful duration prior improves general within-user order.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: -0.0005 to +0.0018 if duration-driven top-five inversions are reduced.
